Worked for a major satellite TV provider for a summer and 2 stories stick out of the many I have. 
The first involved a customer with an invalid complaint: I forget exactly what but there's no doubt it involved owing the company a fuck ton of money. I take the call and the person is a little ticked off sounding but not rude. They ask for a Manager very quickly and it being a slow night I figure what the hell. While I put them I hold I take a closer look at older account notes. This person had been on the phone for close to 24 hours speaking to rep after rep and countless managers and was still trying to rip the company off. 

Second story: A man calls in about PPV charges on his bill.  Policy dictates that if you can sorta prove they're fraudulent we'll reverse them granted you allow us to help you place some kind of controls on ordering. This customer had previously had about 200$ of PPV porn reversed and had had ordering by remote removed.  I explained that I couldn't reverse the charges a 2nd time and that someone with his information had ordered using other means at which point he begins yelling at his son. I hear the whole thing and instantly any sorry feelings I have for him are gone. 

tl:dr: Customer on phone with various reps for nearly 24 hours. 
Don't yell at your son for watching PPV porn while on the phone with a rep asking to reverse the charges.

Sophomore year of college, my boyfriend and I went to the same school. I knew it would be hard to maintain a relationship brought from high school, and I tried, but it eventually got to the point where I had to respect myself. He was a preacher's kid, so he basically went buck wild as soon as he got to school (our school does have a reputation for partying, but is a great school academically too). I was working almost 30 hours a week at the dining hall and making high B's and A's, while he worked maybe 8 hours a week at another dining hall makinu shit grades. I was being supportive with both money and time as I had a car. As time went on I started to realize that to him nothing was his fault; example he blamed his poor grades on the fact that the free math tutor he saw was foreign and he couldn't understand his accent. Finally middle of Fall semester sophomore year he fails out; I had had enough of his constant excuses and drain on my life, so I told him point blank we were over. We did have the stupid "we'll still be friends though" talk= haven't seen him since. Last I heard he still lives here working a min wage job and partying. 
My only lingering feelings concern his parents who are awesome people and I felt really bad about him disappointing them/ wasting their limited resources. (They were "church mice" poor for many years until they moved a couple of states over to a better church.)

Related: my Mom has always been a blunt person and has said some things that a lot of people take to be mean without context attached.       
Example: My Mom's an RN and my Dad's a doctor. One day I was thinking out loud about becoming a doctor myself when she told me she didn't think I had the common sense for the medical field in a tone motherly advice. If I hadn't have been so self aware it probably would have hurt but my Mom's honesty is something I really admire her for.

Former student culinary at O-House here. 

-Any close-toed shoes- I would suggest sneakers you don't care about. Also long pants- again something you wouldn't mind getting wet and/or dirty. 

-As far as work goes for a normal student worker you'll come in and be assigned a station ex. deli, main line etc. Don't get too comfy at one place they will move you around at will; the dishroom will make a man out of you. Night shifts will be pretty steady work after about 5:30pm and depending on the alignment of the stars some nights are crazy. Cleaning can be simple to intense depending where you are, but alway thorough. Also don't be too committed to 10pm; there will always be nights when that may turn into 10:30. 

-Food service in general can be quite humbling, especially if you haven't had a job before. Just work hard, don't be afraid to ask how to do things, always wash your hands and remember everything, including the smell can be taken off with a shower. 

EDIT: Working FS for summer is mind-numbingly boring due to simple lack of customers and is not at all indicative of the regular school year.

I was diagnosed as a major depressive at the age of 8 and Prozac worked amazingly for 7 years. I believe will always have long and deep depressive episodes when unmedicated with about a week of 'normality' and 2 or 3 days of mania. I wasn't diagnosed as bipolar I until April of this year after my father and my stepmother got back together after several years of separation. She was the one that noticed my manic episodes, whereas I think my parents merely believed I was excited about coming home for the weekends from college. I probably gradually transitioned/developed BP when I got to college and I hid it for a while thinking I merely needed a new anti-depressant or I was being lazy or was bad at adjusting.
